housing: Stratford-on-Avon is a large rural district with the highest average house price in the West Midlands. Private renting is below the national average, with lets concentrated in Stratford-upon-Avon itself and the market towns. Many homes are listed timber-framed or stone cottages in conservation areas, while the towns and larger villages have grown with big new-build estates. Tourism and the theatre bring short lets and some staff housing in the town.
checkinTips: Timber-framed and listed cottages: photograph beams, uneven floors, small leaded or single-glazed windows and any cracks in plaster.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank or LPG bottles, the fuel level and the boiler service label.
Homes with wood burners or open fires: photograph the stove, glass, hearth and the chimney sweep certificate.
New-build estates in Wellesbourne, Southam and Shipston: note snagging marks, garden fences, turf and parking spaces.
Cottages near the River Avon and Stour: check ground floors and walls for damp or past flood marks.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Stratford-on-Avon District Council's Private Sector Housing team about disrepair, damp and unsafe conditions.
